conventions.convention: Integers n,p≥1; X is fixed; the parameter set is all of R^p; Y is the identity observation on Euclidean Borel R^n, with integrable coordinates and EβY=Xβ. No covariance, independence, Gaussianity, or design-selection law is imposed.
Least squares denotes the entire argmin set of the squared Euclidean residual norm; it does not select a coefficient vector.
A contrast is any c^Tβ with c∈R^p. Linear estimability requires one deterministic a, independent of the response and unknown parameter, satisfying unbiasedness for every β∈R^p.
The classical covariance and BLUE results assume full column rank and covariance σ²I_n with a fixed σ²>0; BLUE minimizes variance within linear unbiased estimators, without a Gaussian assumption.

load_bearing.statement: A fixed-design first-moment linear regression model has fixed X∈R^{n×p}, n,p≥1, parameter set R^p, observation space Euclidean Borel R^n, integrable response coordinates, and EβY=Xβ for every β.

For n,p≥1, X∈R^{n×p}, and y∈R^n, the least-squares solution set is nonempty, is characterized by X^T(Xb−y)=0, and equals b₀+ker X for any minimizer b₀. Every minimizer has fitted vector P_col(X)y and residual y−P_col(X)y; dim ker X=p−rank(X). No statistical assumption is required.

In a fixed-design first-moment regression model, c^Tβ is linearly estimable if and only if c∈row(X)=im(X^T), equivalently if and only if X^Ta=c for some a∈R^n. Every such a^TY is unbiased for every β.

In the fixed-design first-moment model, if X has full column rank and the errors have finite second moments, mean zero, and covariance σ²I_n for every β, with σ²>0, the unique least-squares estimator is (X^TX)⁻¹X^TY, is unbiased, and has covariance σ²(X^TX)⁻¹.
For n≥1 and a∈R^n, y↦a^Ty is measurable from Euclidean Borel R^n to Borel R.

For a full-column-rank fixed-design first-moment model with error covariance σ²I_n, σ²>0, every OLS contrast is unbiased and has variance no larger than any other linear unbiased estimator of that contrast. Gaussianity is not assumed.

alerts.finding: In Remarks, def-euclidean-inner-product says the general theory of inner product spaces, including orthogonal projection and orthogonal complements, “is planned for a page of this library that comes **earlier in the plan order** and is not yet built.” This is stale: the opened published items def-orthogonal-projection and thm-orthogonal-projection-is-the-unique-nearest-point already define and prove abstract finite-dimensional orthogonal projection, and the batch legitimately uses them. The mathematical definition is unaffected.

seams_checked.note: The model definition and page explicitly describe only abstract model-side fields, acknowledge the absent application and target population, and make no scientific adequacy claim. This respects the supplier's specified-analysis contract requirements.

The exact-inference theorem F14–F17 faithfully restates the first-moment model, least-squares definition, unique fitted vector, and row-space criterion. Its Gaussian, full-rank, and positive residual-degree assumptions are supplied separately; its uses satisfy the regression interfaces.

This is a contextual page prerequisite. The PCA page and its current item dependency declarations contain no direct citation to an assigned regression item and make no stronger claim attributed to regression.

The mixed-model and GLS definitions preserve fixed X and the first-moment convention. The GLS BLUE theorem accurately cites full-rank Gauss–Markov and verifies its hypotheses after whitening, with transformed covariance I_n and no Gaussian assumption.

The page and finite-population definition correctly state that fixed-design regression assigns no selection law to X and therefore supplies no sampling design on population units. They preserve the distinction between design probability and a fixed regression matrix.
